requirements.evidence: Data model, policies, pick controller, routes, lang keys and the three Livewire pages are all there: migration has `storedAs("CASE WHEN `role` = 'owner' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END")` + unique `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:21-22); pick returns 403 when there is no membership, writes to the `audit` channel and then redirects (EntityPickController.php:16-27); transfer checks the target is an admin of this entity and not the caller, and that the owner row exists, then uses a DB::transaction (Settings.php:77-104); removeMember protects the owner and the last manager (Members.php:85-100). Gaps: assignRole lets anyone change the owner's membership, so the owner can be demoted to admin/employee and the entity ends up with no owner (Members.php:61-74); UserRole::manageable() is defined but the code uses the hard-coded 'in:admin,employee' instead (Members.php:68); there is no wire:confirm on delete even though the text asks 'Delete this entity?' (settings.blade.php:53-54).

conventions.evidence: The diff has no tests at all, which breaks the 'no production code without a test' rule. Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, save, delete, transfer) happen inline in Livewire components rather than in app/Actions/* classes (Members.php:50, Settings.php:46, 58-60, 101-104). Settings `$name`/`$slug` have no #[Validate] attribute and use inline `$this->validate([...])` instead (Settings.php:22-24, 41-44). Members uses `Validator::make` instead of the component pattern (Members.php:66-69). EntityPickController uses a manual `abort(403)` rather than the policy (EntityPickController.php:16-18). Positives: policies are registered (AppServiceProvider.php:30-31), $fillable is set, migrations have reversible down(), and docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md were updated. Some screen text is hard-coded rather than coming from lang ('admin'/'employee' buttons, raw `$membership->role->value`) (members.blade.php:33-36).

security.evidence: This is an exploitable privilege flaw: EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole only checks that the caller is owner/admin (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:16-21), and Members::assignRole never checks the target's current role (Members.php:61-74). An admin can call `assignRole(<ownerMembershipId>, 'employee')` and demote the owner, which leaves the entity with no owner and takes settings/billing control away from the owner. Otherwise authorization is solid: every action calls authorize server-side, membership IDs are resolved through `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail(...)` so another entity's IDs can't be used, `#[Locked] public Entity $entity` stops the entity from being swapped, all output uses {{ }}, and models set $fillable.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files under tests/. Nothing covers the policies, the DB one-owner constraint, the pick endpoint, or the Livewire actions, including the unauthorized-call and tamper tests the Livewire policy requires.

simplicity.evidence: The code is generally direct and doesn't add service layers. Some redundancy: delete() and transfer() call authorize, re-fetch with `Entity::findOrFail($this->entity->id)` and then authorize again (Settings.php:52-56, 71-75), and transfer re-checks the owner's user_id even though manageSettings already guarantees it (Settings.php:93-99). The `$membership->role === UserRole::Owner` check in removeMember repeats the policy (Members.php:87-89), and `$isManager` still includes Owner even though the owner was already excluded (Members.php:91).

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short, with PHPDoc generics on relations and typed returns. Small blemishes: the `$name` variable in EntityFactory.php:20 is set and used only once, assignRole uses a ternary to map role strings to the enum instead of `UserRole::from($role)` (Members.php:72), and there are `@param mixed` docblocks for untyped IDs.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: models, enum, policies, factories, migrations, controller, Livewire components/views, routes, lang, docs and changelog. Nothing out of scope (onboarding, switcher, middleware, navbar) was added.

issues.explanation: The change has no Pest/PHPUnit tests, which violates the mandatory TDD convention and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each action).
assignRole never refuses to act on the owner's membership, so an admin can demote the owner to employee and leave the entity with no owner.
Domain writes are done inline in Livewire components instead of in app/Actions/* use-case classes as the conventions require.
Settings `name`/`slug` lack #[Validate] attributes and Members uses Validator::make, both departing from the project's #[Validate] + $this->validate() pattern.
Role validation hard-codes 'in:admin,employee' instead of using the contract's UserRole::manageable(), so manageable() is dead code.
The role labels and the 'admin'/'employee' button texts are hard-coded rather than coming from lang/*/ui.php.
Authorization uses a manual membership check and abort(403) instead of `$this->authorize('view', $entity)` through EntityPolicy.
The delete button acts immediately with no wire:confirm or dialog, even though the confirm text is displayed, so a misclick deletes the entity.
The entity is re-fetched and authorized twice, and the owner user_id is re-checked after manageSettings already guarantees it.

review.summary: The change builds the entities/memberships data model with a portable one-owner DB constraint, the policies, the pick endpoint and the dashboard/members/settings Livewire pages, with docs and changelog updated and good scope discipline. It cannot be approved: there are no tests at all, an admin can demote the owner through assignRole, and domain writes skip the project's Actions layer.
